title: Unaccompanied Minors
full_review:
This holiday season, there have already been two Christmas clunkers -- "Deck the Halls" and "The Santa Clause 3" -- that, someday when available on DVD, could replace lumps of coal as the stocking stuffer for naughty boys and girls. Now comes "Unaccompanied Minors" (Warner Bros.), quite possibly the worst of the lot.

Director Paul Feig's comedy centers on early-teen Spencer (Dyllan Christopher), who gets separated from his little sister, Katherine (Dominique Saldana), while waylaid at an airport during a Christmas Eve blizzard. They are traveling alone from their home in California, where they live with their mom, Valerie (Paget Brewster), to spend Christmas with their divorced dad, Sam (Rob Corddry), in Pennsylvania.

When Katherine is shuttled -- along with an unruly horde of other unaccompanied minors -- to a hotel until the weather clears, Spencer, who escaped the chaotic holding pen, recruits several other stranded juveniles (Gina Mantegna, Tyler James Williams, Brett Kelly and Quinn Shephard) to help him reunite with Katherine in time for Christmas morning.

Standing in their way is the airport's Scrooge-like security chief, Oliver Porter (Lewis Black).

Much mayhem and slapstick silliness lead to a contrived sentimental payoff. The inanity insults the intelligence of youngsters and will be a chore for grown-ups "accompanying" their minors.

The film contains some mildly crude language and humor, as well as divorce themes. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is A-II -- adults and adolescents. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is PG -- parental guidance suggested. Some material may not be suitable for children.
